title: A heel-to-head push diagonal needs a whole-body tilt
summary: Hinge + lean still looked upright for a cart pusher: the reference is a straight heel-to-head line. Widest-stride clip + a whole-body tilt about the rear foot, then hand IK.

versions.note: seed harvest of the shot-match scenes (L3)

usage.example: tilt(pusher, .45);   // once in build; tick: Walk_Loop t 0, hinge .22, lean .12, handTo the rim

doc.when: Pushing, leaning into wind, bracing against a door.
doc.avoid: Trying to get the diagonal from the spine alone.
gotchas: The tilted feet are not checked against the floor: look at them.

params.pivot: .25 m per rad behind the origin

problem.symptom: The pusher looks upright even with hinge + lean.
problem.cause: The diagonal runs through the legs; spine bones can't make it.
problem.fix: Walk_Loop at its widest stride + group.rotateX(tilt) pivoted near the rear foot + hand IK.
problem.detect: Side view: the heel-hip-head line is not straight.
